title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (cote 143, c.1980-81; this is the anabelian programme just before the Esquisse). X is a variety, essentially over Q, with a profinite 'symmetry group' 𝔊_X mapping to Γ = Gal(Q̄/Q). The group 𝔊_X probably mixes Galois elements and Q̄-automorphisms of X. The previous page shows how a point ξ gives a 'genre' (germ) of section. That is, a section defined only up to restriction to an open subgroup Γ' ⊂ Γ and up to conjugation by π_1.

On the previous page Grothendieck introduces:
- a divisor D = Σ_{i∈I} D_i on X, with normal crossings, no multiple components, and X regular at the generic points of the D_i;
- the open complement X' = X − supp D;
- the subgroup 𝔊_{X'} (more precisely 𝔊_X(I)) of elements stabilising D.

This page:
- (14) An extension 1 → π_1(X') → E_{X'} → 𝔊_{X'} → 1. Here π_1(X') is the geometric (profinite) fundamental group of X'_{Q̄}, and E_{X'} is the 'arithmetic' fundamental group adapted to 𝔊_{X'}. Hence the outer action 𝔊_{X'} → Out(π_1(X')).
- Germs of lifts ('relèvements circonstanciels'), defined modulo conjugation by inner automorphisms coming from π_1(X').
- (15) A point ξ ∈ X'(Q̄), defined over the fixed field of an open Γ' ⊂ Γ, gives a section φ_ξ: Γ' → E_{X'} over Γ' ⊂ Γ. It is well defined up to π_1(X')-conjugacy and shrinking Γ'.
- (16) Since 𝔊_{X'} stabilises D, it permutes the components: 𝔊_{X'} → 𝔖_I.
- (17) Kummer theory (tame ramification along the generic point of D_i) gives, for every i, an exterior homomorphism φ_i: T(Q̄) = lim μ_n(Q̄) = Ẑ(1) → π_1(X'). This is the conjugacy class of the inertia subgroup at D_i ('loop around D_i').
- (18) The cyclotomic character χ: Γ → Ẑ^* ≅ Aut(Ẑ(1)) lets 𝔊_{X'} act on T via Γ.
- The statement begun here and finished on the next page: the outer action of 𝔊_{X'} on π_1(X') respects the family (φ_i), its 'Kummerian structures'. For g ∈ 𝔊_{X'}, g∘φ_i = φ_{σ(g)(i)}∘χ(g) up to conjugacy. This yields (19) 𝔊_{X'} → Autext(π_1(X'), T(Q̄), (φ_i)).
- The next page refines this. It passes from conjugacy classes to the π_1-sets of inertia/decomposition data above the D_i, via the normalisation of X in the universal pro-cover of X'.

Purpose: to encode the arithmetic of an open variety (e.g. a punctured curve or moduli space) in a profinite group with extra 'cuspidal/inertia' structure. Galois and automorphism actions then land in a restricted outer-automorphism group. This is the key structure used later to define 'inertia-preserving' (braid-like) outer automorphisms.
errors: The φ_i need not be injective (e.g. one point removed from P^1 gives trivial inertia), so 'hom' rather than embedding is correct. But the later structure Autext(π_1, T, (φ_i)) can degenerate for such D_i; Grothendieck does not discuss this.

The compatibility involves both the permutation σ(g) and the cyclotomic twist χ(g). When 𝔊_{X'} contains geometric automorphisms acting trivially on Γ, only the permutation enters. This is implicit, not spelled out.

The φ_i are well defined only up to π_1(X')-conjugacy (exterior homs). Making them literal homomorphisms requires choosing points above D_i in the pro-cover, which the next page begins to do. On this page the compatibility statement is therefore only a statement on conjugacy classes.
The Kummer/tame description of inertia as a quotient of Ẑ(1) is valid in characteristic 0 (here over Q̄). Over positive or mixed characteristic only the tame part would be Ẑ'(1).

ideas.what: Extension 1→π_1(X')→E_{X'}→𝔊_{X'}→1 and sections from rational points, defined up to conjugacy and restriction to open subgroups ('genre'/germ of section)
ideas.modern_name: fundamental exact sequence / Galois sections of arithmetic fundamental groups (section conjecture setting)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 IX for the sequence; Letter to Faltings 1983 for the section conjecture)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. IX–X; Letter to Faltings (1983); Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

ideas.what: Inertia at components of a normal crossings divisor as exterior homomorphisms Ẑ(1)→π_1(X') via Kummer theory
ideas.modern_name: tame inertia subgroups / cuspidal inertia; 'loops around the boundary divisor'

ideas.what: The outer Galois/symmetry action preserves the family of inertia classes, up to permutation of components and the cyclotomic twist: 𝔊_{X'}→Autext(π_1(X'), T, (φ_i)) ('structures kummériennes')
ideas.modern_name: inertia-preserving / 'braid-like' outer automorphisms (Out^♯, Out^* in Ihara–Nakamura), cuspidal outer automorphisms (Mochizuki, Hoshi–Mochizuki)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Nakamura (late 1980s–1990s), Drinfeld/Ihara for GT conditions; Mochizuki for cuspidal structures
ideas.where_published: Spirit present in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, divisors at infinity); explicit formalisation unsure

ideas.what: Group 𝔊_X mixing Galois elements and automorphisms of X, with stabiliser of D and induced permutation of components
ideas.modern_name: semidirect/extended 'arithmetic symmetry group' acting on π_1 (e.g. Γ × S_n acting on π_1(M_{0,n}))
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (implicitly, for moduli M_{g,n} with S_n action)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formalises, c.1980, the requirement that outer Galois (and symmetry) actions preserve inertia classes at the boundary divisor, twisted by permutation of components and by the cyclotomic character. He names these 'structures kummériennes' and defines the target group Autext(π_1(X'), T(Q̄), (φ_i)). This is essentially the inertia-preservation condition later central to Ihara–Nakamura's work on Out of moduli fundamental groups and to the GT-type conditions. It appears here in general form for any normal-crossings complement, before those works.
missed.quote: La théorie de Kummer nous fournit, pour tout i, un hom extérieur T(Q̄) →φ_i π_1(X') ... l'opération extérieure de 𝔊_{X'} sur π_1(X') est compatible avec la famille des (φ_i) ("structures Kummériennes")
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority note for the inertia-preserving condition in anabelian geometry. The idea is standard now, but this page documents that Grothendieck had the general formulation (arbitrary NCD complement, symmetry group beyond Galois) by c.1980.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics consists of standard tame-ramification and outer-action facts that Grothendieck himself founded. The general formulation of Kummerian/inertia structures preserved by Galois/symmetry actions is a mildly interesting early anabelian detail. It is not a missed result, since the condition is well known (Ihara, Nakamura, Mochizuki).
transcription_corrections: Line after (14): likely 'et on a encore un genre de relèvements circonstanciels mod conj. par automorphismes int. provenant de π_1(X')' — 'genre' (germ), not 'groupe'; 'hom' struck and replaced by 'relèvements'(?).
(15): the diagram is E_{X'} → 𝔊_{X'} → Γ ⊃ Γ', with a diagonal arrow φ_ξ from Γ' back to E_{X'}.
'Notons prime ici un hom' is probably 'Notons qu'on a ici un hom'.
'pour [?] i' is probably 'pour tout i' ('pour tt i').
(17): the right-hand note reads φ_i ∈ Homext(T(Q̄), π_1(X')). Below T(Q̄) is the definition T(Q̄) = lim← μ_n(Q̄).
'l'[-opération-] {+opération+} extérieure' — the struck word is probably 'Opération' rewritten, so read simply 'l'opération extérieure de 𝔊_{X'} sur π_1(X')'.
Script 𝔊_{X'} (fraktur/script G) is used throughout, consistently with the previous page.
